facts.fact: Landinfo states that responsibility for civil registration lies with the General Directorate for Civil Registration under the Ministry of Interior, which also issues birth certificates; the report gives no date for this beyond its own, so its publication date is used.

Landinfo states that a child's birth is registered in the civil registry, the centralised electronic registry introduced in 2011, and that the birth certificate carries machine-written information and a QR code; officials of the General Directorate told the Norwegian Embassy in 2021 that hand-written certificates are no longer issued. Deaths are not covered in the held excerpt.

Landinfo describes a centralised electronic civil registry that in 2011 replaced hand-written, decentralised registers, in which registration is possible at any civil registry office in the country and births are registered on application at a civil registry office against a paper notice of birth; it does not spell out at which desk the birth entry is keyed, and gives no date beyond its own, so its publication date is used.

systems.country_label: civil registry (General Directorate for Civil Registration)
systems.owner: General Directorate for Civil Registration, Ministry of Interior
systems.tiers: central registry reached from civil registry offices nationwide (registration possible at any office); registration offices in all major cities in Darfur, none in IDP settlements, and some offices burnt down; birth certificate issued on application with a notice of birth and both parents' national identity numbers; some embassies issue birth certificates

systems.system: national identity number and civil registration certificate
systems.owner: General Directorate for Civil Registration, Ministry of Interior
systems.tiers: in-person enrolment at a registration point with fingerprints and photograph; 11-digit number; officials reported 82% of the population registered in 2016 and 35.5 million of 40 million by 2021; a father applies for a child's number with the birth certificate until age 12, so the number is not issued by the birth registration itself; also at embassies with biometric equipment
more than a thousand units dispatched for the 2011 mass registration into the new civil registry; mobile teams have occasionally visited embassies

systems.owner: health institution, or midwife or parents for a birth outside one
systems.tiers: paper notice given to the parents with a copy sent to the local authorities within 15 days (Civil Registry Act 2011, arts. 20 and 21); no digital tool described

note: Held text is an excerpt ending in section 2.3; sections on the ID card, passports and document reliability are not held. For the rural flag: the report cites MICS 2014 that 67% of under-fives were registered, 89% in urban areas against 59% in rural, and under 50% in the Darfur states - shares of births, not of offices.
